What this place is

A mountain tavern that never got polished up

In the owner's own words: “Food, libations and a warm welcome.” Tap any heading to see what's behind it.

  • Walls and ceiling papered in signed dollar bills, left by people passing through.
  • A pool table under green shaded lamps in the middle of it.
  • It’s the first thing most people mention — you sign a dollar, and it goes up with the rest.

  • Ten taps, wine, and a full-service bar.
  • Hand-dipped milkshakes if you're driving on.
  • The taps and the nachos are what regulars order together.

  • Prime rib every Friday night — the owner's own standing line about this place.
  • Weekday nightly specials run through the week as well.
  • Homemade chili by the bowl, all week: “Always good food, homemade chili and great service.”

  • The old couch in front of a giant rock fireplace.
  • A back room that's family friendly, and a yard out back with extra seating in summer.
  • Boots off the trail welcome — the wall sign only draws the line at caulk boots.

What people say

Word of mouth, mile marker to mile marker

The tavern on 410

Historically the Naches Tavern. Still is.

The sign out front says Naches Tavern. The listings say Naches Bar and Grill. It's the same building, the same bar, and the same room full of dollar bills.

It sits at 58411 Highway 410, out past Greenwater, on the only road between Enumclaw and Crystal Mountain. Skiers in winter, hikers in summer, and the people who live up here year round all end up at the same handful of tables. Since the Fairfax Bridge closed, locals have been asking people to keep stopping in.

“Food, libations and a warm welcome,” is how the owner describes it — platter-sized Naches Nachos piled high, great hamburgers, salads, chili, weekday nightly specials, Friday prime rib, hand-dipped milkshakes, ten beers on tap, a full-service bar, and the famous old couch in front of a giant rock fireplace.

And no, not Naches near Yakima. This one's on the mountain.

Coming up the hill

Pull in, we're easy to spot

  1. Watch for the neon

    Red neon on a dark cedar A-frame, string lights along the porch, and a tall carved wooden figure standing by the door.

  2. Park anywhere along the shoulder

    Everyone does. The lot fills first on ski weekends and summer afternoons.

  3. Grab a table or the couch

    Bar, family room in the back, or the yard out back when it's warm. Order at the bar.
